messages.author: bebd85531a67ef86
messages.subject: sum with decreasing indices
parts:
Dear nimble users

Is this known nimble behaviour? The un-compiled and compiled versions of this function give different output. 

test = nimbleFunction(
  run = function(x=double(1)) {
    n = length(x)
    nimPrint(sum(x[1:n]))
    nimPrint(sum(x[n:1]))
  }
)

cTest = compileNimble(test)

test   (1:6)    # Prints 21 twice  - the expected output
cTest(1:6)    # Prints 21 and 6  - somewhat surprising output 

Best regards
David

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: sum with decreasing indices
parts:
hi David,

We haven't implemented negative indexing on the C++ side. It's documented in Table 11.1 of the User Manual, but that is of course buried in a rather long document...

We should probably emit a warning or error if one tries to do this. I'll file an issue.

-Chris

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: sum with decreasing indices
parts: Yes, this is one of those discrepancies for which, at run-time, if it is sum(x[n1:n2]) where n1 and n2 are run-time values, it would be a bit tricky to trap cases where uncompiled (pure R) execution is different due to n2 < n1.  Maybe we should support decreasing indices in compilation.  I'm forgetting why we didn't.  Possibly out of caution.  Possibly because decreasing indices are not supported in models (although that is quite a different context).
